scope: Warm local TTS runs (three seeds per condition); synthetic browser microphone through HTTPS (three requests), no physical mic or device latency. Different seeds/numerics can produce different durations.
codec_correctness: On three fixed seeds, BF16 waveforms were bit-identical with and without codec graphs. Reference copy cache: 262.9 ms initial encode, 0.6 ms on subsequent copies.
limitations: BF16 and different sampling random streams can change outputs. Four zero-WER fixtures are not a comprehensive naturalness or speaker-identity evaluation. One cold-load compiled sampler failed on torch 2.6, so its flag is off; Triton local decode is enabled. First PCM can contain leading silence: in three positive-temperature quality probes the first nonquiet chunk arrived at approximately 127–139 ms. Browser results exclude physical device latency. Preliminary mouth-to-ear values counted an internal pause as speech end and are superseded by the final runs.
